paper_metadata.title: Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks with Amplitude Encoding for Credit Recovery Rate Prediction

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical recovery rate regression using amplitude encoding on a 256-feature proprietary credit dataset, evaluated against classical FNN and angle-encoding QML baselines under cross-validation and LOOCV.

algorithm.variant: Hybrid QML with Amplitude Encoding and Strongly Entangling PQC
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 100 epochs; best test RMSE selected during training

hyperparameters.PQC_gate_structure: single-qubit R(α,β,γ) rotations followed by range-1 CNOT entangling layer
hyperparameters.measurement: expectation values of Z Pauli observables

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 256 classical features are normalized and encoded into amplitudes of an 8-qubit quantum state; requires n = log2(256) = 8 qubits
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize RMSE for recovery rate regression

problem_instance.description: Predict bond recovery rate (bond price 30 days after default) from firm-, bond-, credit-risk-, industry-, and macroeconomic features.
problem_instance.dataset_name: NRF Research Project UP5 / CRI recovery rate dataset

dataset_specification.description: 1,725 observations covering 576 firms from 1996 to 2023; recovery rate defined as bond price 30 days after default; continuous features standardized with z-score normalization using training-set statistics only; categorical True/False features mapped to 0/1; no PCA; four-fold cross-validation with fold-specific preprocessing and LOOCV used for evaluation.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical neural preprocessing layer with input and hidden layer of equal size; LeakyReLU activation; z-score normalization for continuous features; binary mapping for categorical features.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Final classical output layer maps measured quantum expectation values to recovery-rate prediction.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports faster training than the angle-encoding QML variant (0.73 s vs 0.81 s per epoch), but does not claim a formal speedup over classical models because classical and quantum runs used different hardware (CPU simulator vs GPU).

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical recovery rate regression using angle encoding with an auxiliary classical layer, evaluated on the same 256-feature proprietary dataset.

algorithm.variant: QML with Angle Encoding and Strongly Entangling PQC
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 100 epochs; best test RMSE selected during training

hyperparameters.PQC_gate_structure: single-qubit Rx rotations followed by range-1 CNOT entangling layer
hyperparameters.measurement: expectation values of Z Pauli observables

problem_formulation.encoding_details: A classical auxiliary layer reduces the 256 input features to 8 values, which are then encoded as rotation angles on 8 qubits using Rx gates.
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize RMSE for recovery rate regression
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: auxiliary classical dimensionality reduction to match qubit count

problem_instance.description: Predict bond recovery rate from the same 256-feature credit-risk dataset.
problem_instance.dataset_name: NRF Research Project UP5 / CRI recovery rate dataset

dataset_specification.description: Same dataset and preprocessing as exp_1; evaluated with four-fold cross-validation and LOOCV.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical preprocessing layer with input and hidden layer of equal size; LeakyReLU activation; auxiliary layer reduces dimensionality to 8 outputs before angle encoding.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Final classical output layer maps measured quantum expectation values to recovery-rate prediction.

speedup_claims.caveats: Angle-encoding QML is slower than the FNN in simulation (0.81 s vs 0.03 s per epoch), but the paper explicitly states that direct runtime comparisons between classical GPU training and CPU-based quantum simulation are not meaningful.

experiments.description: Control experiment: orthogonality-constrained fully connected neural network for recovery rate prediction on the same dataset, used to isolate the effect of unitary/orthogonal regularization from the quantum layer.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 100 epochs; best test RMSE selected during training

hyperparameters.orthogonal_projection: SVD projection W = UΣV^T, then W <- UV^T after each gradient step

problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize RMSE for recovery rate regression
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: orthogonality enforced by projecting hidden-layer weights onto the orthogonal factor after each update

problem_instance.description: Same recovery-rate regression task as the QML models, using the 256-feature proprietary credit dataset.
problem_instance.dataset_name: NRF Research Project UP5 / CRI recovery rate dataset

dataset_specification.description: Same dataset and preprocessing as exp_1; evaluated with four-fold cross-validation and LOOCV.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Input layer and hidden layer of equal size; LeakyReLU activation; standard z-score normalization and binary mapping preprocessing as in the main experiments.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Final classical output layer for regression; hidden-layer weights orthogonalized after each gradient step.

speedup_claims.caveats: The orthogonal network is a classical control baseline; no speedup claim is made. It is slower than the FNN in simulation (0.15 s vs 0.03 s per epoch) due to SVD-based orthogonal projection after each update.

experiments.description: Preliminary noisy-hardware and noisy-simulator experiment for angle-encoding QML on a reduced 32-feature dataset, including a real QPU run on Rigetti Ankaa-3.

algorithm.variant: QML with Angle Encoding on noisy simulator and real QPU
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 13 epochs on hardware-constrained reduced dataset

hyperparameters.PQC_gate_structure: single-qubit Rx rotations followed by entangling layer

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 32 input features are reduced to 5 outputs by a classical auxiliary layer and encoded into 5 qubits via Rx rotations.
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize RMSE for recovery rate regression
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: dimensionality reduction to fit available qubits

problem_instance.description: Reduced-scale recovery-rate prediction experiment for feasibility testing on noisy simulator and real quantum hardware.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Reduced subset of NRF Research Project UP5 / CRI recovery rate dataset

dataset_specification.description: 100 samples, 32 features; single train/test split with 75% training and 25% testing; used only for preliminary hardware feasibility testing.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical auxiliary layer reduces 32 features to 5 inputs for angle encoding; same preprocessing style as main angle-encoding model.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classical output layer for regression after quantum measurement.

speedup_claims.caveats: This is a preliminary feasibility test on a reduced dataset. The paper states that both noisy simulation and a single real-QPU run outperform the classical FNN during the first 13 epochs, but no formal speedup is claimed.

experiments.description: Noisy-simulator feasibility test for the full amplitude-encoding QML model on the 256-feature dataset.

algorithm.variant: QML with Amplitude Encoding on noisy simulator
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 100 epochs on the full dataset

hyperparameters.PQC_gate_structure: single-qubit R(α,β,γ) rotations followed by range-1 CNOT entangling layer

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 256-dimensional input vector encoded into an 8-qubit amplitude state using the Möttönen state-preparation protocol.
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize RMSE for recovery rate regression
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: state-preparation via amplitude encoding; padding/zero-filling discussed as necessary when feature dimension is not a power of two, though not needed here

problem_instance.description: Full recovery-rate prediction task evaluated under a noisy simulator to assess NISQ feasibility.
problem_instance.dataset_name: NRF Research Project UP5 / CRI recovery rate dataset

dataset_specification.description: Same 1,725-observation dataset as the main experiment; noisy-simulator run used the full dataset and a single train/test split in the appendix discussion.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical preprocessing layer before amplitude encoding; z-score normalization for continuous features and 0/1 mapping for categorical features.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classical output layer after quantum measurement.

speedup_claims.caveats: The noisy-simulator appendix reports that the amplitude-encoding model shows only minor deviations from the noiseless model, but no speedup claim is made.
